notes: Electric-dryer parts from the WED94HEXW1 technical sheet, which also covers the gas dryer; gas-only parts are left out. On the electric dryer the inlet thermistor is part of the high thermostat assembly.

gaps: No heater watts or heater resistance for this model; the 50 ohm figure on page 14 is a limit in the heater check, not a heater rating.
No OEM part numbers: the sheet has no parts list.
Left out: 5400 W and 2700 W heater and 1/3 hp motor figures from Whirlpool tech sheet W10042930, which does not name WED94HEXW1.
Gas-only items on these pages (gas valve, ignitor, gas inlet thermistor) are left out.
Water valve and water nozzle are named on page 26 without ratings or a stated use.
Inlet thermistor table (page 16) trimmed to one reference point; the table is not copied.
Supply 240 V, 30 A is the dryer's specification on page 26, put on the power cord named in Test 2 (page 10); the sheet does not rate the cord itself.
Component locations page 26 lists parts by access panel; locations were not claimed because the text order is fragmented.
method: Whirlpool Technical Sheet W10306459B for WED94HEXW1 (ManualsLib, 56 pages) read through the ManualsLib viewer: cover and contents, then viewer pages 5, 10, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19 and 26.

Page 10 is Test 2 (supply connections, power cord). Page 14 is the electric no-heat checks. Page 15 is the heater relay and outlet thermistor. Page 16 is the thermistor tables. Page 18 is the moisture sensor test. Page 19 is the door switch test. Page 26 is component locations and specifications.
The ManualsLib text splits table columns and lines; the inlet thermistor table was lined up by position (7 temperatures, 7 values per column) and only one point is used.
No bot check, login wall or paywall on any page read.
Whirlpool's own site, PartSelect, Fix.com, Sears PartsDirect and whirlpoolparts.com refused or timed out for the researcher and are not cited.

comps.spec: Electric heater assembly; the no-heat check tests continuity across each heater, from its violet wire to the centre red wire.
Heater relay #1, and relay #2 if fitted, on the control unit (CCU); page 15 checks the voltage across each relay's terminals 1 and 2 to tell whether it is open or closed.
High limit thermostat; on the electric dryer the thermal components figure labels it together with the inlet thermistor as one assembly. The no-heat check tests it for continuity.
Thermal cut-off in the heater circuit; the check tests continuity from L1 (P9-2) to the black terminal of each heater relay and replaces the cut-off if it is still open.
Thermal fuse, named on the component locations page.

Inlet thermistor, measured between P14-1 and P14-2 with the connector removed; the electric-dryer table gives 49.0-51.0 kΩ at 77 °F (25 °C). On the electric dryer it is part of the high thermostat assembly.
Outlet (exhaust) thermistor, measured at connector P14 on the CCU between pins 3 and 6; 5-15 kΩ means it is good.
Two metal moisture strips inside the drum, on a 3-wire moisture sensor connector. Test 5 has you clean the strips and replace the sensor harness if a small resistance is still measured.
Drive motor assembly, named 'Motor Assembly & Belt Switch' on the component locations page, which also names a pluggable drive motor switch.
Centrifugal switch on the drive motor (callout 'Centrifugal Switch (Motor)').
Belt switch, listed with the motor assembly in the callout 'Motor Assembly & Belt Switch'.
Door switch. Test 7 is a functional check: opening the door shows the electric display code p6e and turns on the drum light, and closing it turns the light off.
Cycle Control Unit (CCU) and User Interface (UI), named on the component locations page.

Power cord of the electric dryer (Test 2 on page 10 replaces it if a plug terminal has no continuity). The specifications page gives the electric dryer supply as 240 VAC (200-260 V), 2-phase, with 30 A service.
Water valve and water nozzle, both named as components on the component locations page.
